#supplements The user wants supplement write-ups covering pros, cons, body interactions/body parts affected, and natural sources, in a grid/table format, with both a short (~240 character) and long (~500-word) description per supplement. They re-asked several times when the table came out truncated.

#L-CitrullineMalate L-Citrulline Malate 2:1 pairs the amino acid L-Citrulline with malate. Pros: raises nitric oxide and blood flow, improving exercise performance, endurance and recovery, and reducing soreness/fatigue. Cons: stomach discomfort or diarrhea. Natural sources: watermelon (citrulline), apples and other fruit (malate). Malate aids absorption, so plain L-Citrulline without malate is less effective.

#Resveratrol Resveratrol: polyphenol antioxidant and anti-inflammatory, may improve heart health and protect against age-related disease. Cons: may interact with blood thinners and certain medications; long-term effects not fully understood. Natural sources: grapes, peanuts, berries.

#BetaAlanine Beta Alanine: non-essential amino acid that raises muscle carnosine, improving muscular endurance and high-intensity performance and delaying fatigue. Cons: tingling/itching (paresthesia); natural food sources are limited.
#LGlutamine L-Glutamine: amino acid supporting muscle recovery, immune function and gut health, and reducing soreness. Natural sources: protein-rich foods such as meat, fish, eggs and dairy.
#CaseinProtein Casein protein: slow-digesting dairy protein giving sustained amino acid release, ideal overnight for muscle repair and reducing muscle breakdown. Natural sources: milk and cheese.
#EggWhiteProtein Egg white protein: high-quality, easily absorbed, low in calories and fat, good for lean muscle and weight loss and for muscle recovery/growth. Natural source: egg whites.
#BeefProteinIsolate Beef protein isolate: high-quality protein low in fat and cholesterol, used to build lean muscle mass. Natural source: lean beef.
#PapayaSeed Papaya seed: natural source of digestive enzymes that may aid digestion and gut health; rich in magnesium, potassium and calcium; anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties.

#HawthornBerry Hawthorn berry: used for centuries for heart health; antioxidants may lower blood pressure, improve circulation and reduce anxiety; possibly helpful for some digestive and skin conditions.
#Longjack Longjack (Tongkat Ali): may raise testosterone in men, enhance athletic performance and improve sexual health; long traditional use for ailments such as malaria and fever.
#Fenugreek Fenugreek: may increase milk production in breastfeeding mothers, lower cholesterol and improve blood sugar control in diabetes; has anti-inflammatory properties.
#Schisandra Schisandra: traditional Chinese medicine berry; may improve liver function, reduce inflammation and enhance cognitive function; contains antioxidants.

#FoTi Fo-Ti / He Shou Wu: traditional Chinese medicine; may improve hair health, reduce signs of aging and improve fertility; antioxidant-rich, but more research is needed on effects and side effects.
